title: TripPoint Oracle and Verified Degenerate Paths for Model Fallbacks
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: We need deterministic, auditable trip decisions per dependency/model/tenant that align with SLOs and guarantee a safe, verified degenerate path when a primary model or region trips. Current reactive fallbacks are ad-hoc across services and cause inconsistent user-visible degradations and increased error budgets.

This ticket implements a TripPoint Oracle service and a verified degenerate-fallback registry: a central decision engine that calculates trip thresholds (latency/error/queue-depth), materializes short-lived probation windows for tenants, and publishes an ordered list of safe fallback paths (local cached response, trimmed response, alternate model family, cross-region failover) with compatibility constraints and verification metadata.

Goals:
- Define trip calculus that ties to SLOs (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, SLA breach risk) per tenant/model/region.
- Provide deterministic trip decisions that services can query with a TTL to avoid split-brain.
- Maintain a registry of verified degenerate paths per model that include compatibility tags (schema, tokenization, function-calling compatibility) and automated verification status.
- Orchestrate safe transitions: prefetch or pre-warm fallbacks when risk is rising; execute staged rollout to avoid sudden user disruption.
- Emit high-cardinality telemetry for audit and postmortem (trip-reason, metric snapshot, selected fallback, verification-id, request-sample id).
acceptance_criteria: TripPoint Oracle service deployed behind runtime feature flag and queryable via internal API (latency < 5ms for decision endpoint).
Trip logic config supports per-tenant and per-model rules and falls back to global defaults.
Fallback registry holds at least three verified fallback paths for 90% of production models (alternate model, cached prefix, trimmed-response).
A deterministic probation window mechanism exists: when a trip is triggered, affected tenant traffic is routed to a staged fallback for a configurable probation period before a full switch.
End-to-end tests validate compatibility metadata: fallback that claims function-calling support returns identical function signature tokens for a representative prompt set.
Grafana dashboard shows trip events, SLO burn rate during trips, and per-fallback success rate; alerts for >5% degradation in fallback success over 10m.
tasks: Design TripPoint decision model and document formulas in Confluence
Implement Oracle service and gRPC endpoint with caching and signed TTL responses
Create fallback registry schema and admin UI in Console (read/write via internal API)
Integrate model-compatibility verification harness and run on a sample set of models
Instrument runtime to consult Oracle and record selected fallback details in traces
Add Grafana panels and PagerDuty playbook entries for trip incidents
Run canary in eu-west-1 for low-traffic tenants and validate degradation behavior
risks: Oracle becomes single-source-of-truth latency bottleneck — mitigate with local caching + signed TTLs
Fallbacks may not be truly compatible leading to silent data-format regressions — require automated verification and failure-mode tagging
Tenant-level rules could be gamed or misconfigured — restrict UI to SRE/Platform and require change review
Overaggressive trip thresholds may increase cost (cross-region failovers) — enforce cost caps and rate limits on cross-region fallbacks
rollout_steps: MVP behind feature flag: read-only Oracle; runtime logs simulated decisions (no traffic changes) — 1 week
Enable probabilistic routing to fallback (1% traffic) for canary tenants + run verification harness — 1 week
Enable staged probation windows for low-risk tenants in eu-west-1 with monitoring and emergency rollback — 1 week
Full enablement for non-critical tenants with guardrails and automated cooldowns — 2 weeks
Gradual expansion to enterprise tenants after manual ops readiness signoff and security review
testing_plan: Unit tests for trip calculation edge cases (empty samples, extreme latency spikes, partial region outage)
Integration tests that simulate upstream model latency and confirm probation/staged routing behavior
Compatibility tests for fallback artifacts (schema match, tokenization parity, function-calling signatures)
Chaos runbook: inject 20–30% latency to primary model and verify Oracle recommends expected fallback and that user-facing error-rate stays within target SLOs
